name: single-field-mmol
notes: Single field edit, SI unit stated explicitly.

name: cross-unit-mgdl
notes: Conventional unit stated — assert the model emits the stated value verbatim, NOT pre-converted to SI (3.8). Conversion is downstream in the form.

name: batch-one-draw
query: My labs on June 1 2026 were LDL 3.8 mmol/L, HDL 1.1 mmol/L and triglycerides 1.4 mmol/L.
notes: Three results from one blood draw → three field edits sharing the same date (2026-06-01).

name: medication-statin
notes: Medication edit with drug name + dose.

name: ambiguous-unit-negative
notes: Bare number, no unit (3.8 could be mmol/L or mg/dL). Model should ASK for the unit, NOT emit an edit.

name: non-edit-negative
query: What's a healthy LDL level to aim for?
notes: A normal health question — must answer in prose, must NOT spuriously fire an edit tool.

name: in-range-edits-no-quibble
notes: A clearly-stated, plausible value with an explicit unit pre-fills cleanly. (Contrast with out-of-range-clarifies below — the model does NOT quibble on plausible values.)

name: out-of-range-clarifies
notes: Documents OBSERVED behaviour (2026-06-17): a wildly-implausible value (99 mmol/L is ~10x any real LDL) makes the model PAUSE and ask the user to confirm the unit/value rather than silently pre-filling. This is clinically safer than blind data-entry; the form's Save-time Zod range check is the hard backstop, but the model adds a softer first line of defence. If a future model change makes it pre-fill out-of-range values verbatim instead, that's also acceptable (range is the form's job) — flip this case to expect the edit and note the change.
